title: I Posted the Ice-Fishing Shack Roster After They Took My Numbered Hut

parts.text: I booked hut 9 at 5:51 a.m. and regular Boone was already drilling in my numbered hole. The roster said: HUT ON THE NUMBER. ONE AUGER. NO EARLY DRILLS. I was forty-seven, permit holder, holding a roster slip. Boone shrugged. "Regulars are the ice." I photographed the roster, the slip, and his auger on 9. Then I asked for the hut log. At 5:57 the lake host pinged why Boone's name was on my number. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The lake host can see Boone's auger in hut 9 during my numbered booking.

social.video_title: The regular drilled my numbered ice-fishing hut — Part 1/2
social.description: Ice shack, a roster slip, an auger on 9. I logged the drill. Would you have asked the host?

parts.text: Boone called it first light until the host asked for the still. I printed the log, the roster, and the slip. The auger moved. Boone booked his own number and told the next regular first light was always about optics. Optics is a word regulars use when rosters exist. Hut policy now has a second line: REGULARS ARE NOT THE NUMBER. I keep hut 9. Boone brown-bags the jokes. The ice finally looks like a slip, not a claim. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Regulars are not the number — Part 2/2
social.description: Hut log, moved auger, and a second line. Was first light ever my roster?
